verified_claims: Step 1/2 reduction: greedy next term = smallest element of $V_n=\{m:P(m)\text{ transversal of }\mathcal M_n\}$ exceeding $a_n$; $V_n$ = union of divisibility classes of $\prod\tau$ over the blocker $b(\mathcal M_n)$. Independently reproduced; simulator matches brute-force gcd on $a_1\in\{6,15,30,105,210,385,777,4199,2310,249,...\}$.

Step 3: $\mathcal M_n$-driven valid set is decreasing ($V_{n+1}\subseteq V_n$); the eventual $V(\mathcal M_\infty)\subseteq V_n$ for all $n$; every $a_n\in V$ (the whole family $\{P(a_i)\}$ is pairwise intersecting, so $P(a_n)$ hits every $P(a_i)$ hence every member of every $\mathcal M_m$). Therefore the sequence IS the increasing enumeration of $V$ from $a_1$. Verified: seq == sorted($V\cap[a_1,\infty)$) from $n=1$.

Step 4: with $L=\prod(\text{essential primes})$, $V$ is a finite union of residue classes mod $L$, so the increasing enumeration satisfies $a_{n+T}=a_n+L$ for ALL $n\ge1$. Verified from $n=1$ for $a_1=15\Rightarrow L=30,T=8$; $a_1=385\Rightarrow L=43890,T=5088$; $a_1=105\Rightarrow L=210,T=58$ (all spot values reproduce exactly).

Step 7 cofactor identity (EXACT): at each essential entry $j\ge2$, with $\tau^*=$ minimal transversal of $\mathcal M_{j-1}$ contained in $P(a_j)$ and $D=\prod\tau^*$, $a_j=Dk$ with $k=\lfloor a_{j-1}/D\rfloor+1$ exactly, and the new prime $q\mid k$. Independently verified exact on every event for $a_1\in\{6,15,30,105,210,385,777,4199,2310,249,30030,510510\}$.

Lemma A (TERM): $m\in V_n$ and $a_1\le m\le a_n\Rightarrow m$ is a term. Proof re-derived and correct (V decreasing $\Rightarrow m\in V_i$ for all $i\le n$; a non-term $m\in(a_s,a_{s+1})$ with $a_{s+1}\le a_n$ would give $a_{s+1}\le m<a_{s+1}$). 0 failures on $a_1\in\{6,15,30,105,210,385\}$ (every valid $m\in[a_1,a_n]$ checked).

Lemma B (smooth-gap): consecutive $S$-smooth numbers have ratio $\le\min S$ (else $\min S\cdot n_i$ is $S$-smooth strictly between); so the smallest $S$-smooth $>X$ ($X\ge1$) is $\le(\min S)X$. Proof sound; used with $p_1=\min\tau^*\le D$ to bound the constructed cofactor $c\le a_1$.

Lemma C (B-monotonicity): $B_n=\{M\in\mathcal M_n:M\subseteq\tau^*\}$ never goes nonempty$\to$empty. Three-case analysis ($S\nsubseteq\tau^*$ / $S\subseteq\tau^*$ added / not added) re-derived and correct. 0 nonempty$\to$empty transitions across all snapshots and all events for $a_1\in\{6,15,30,105,210,385\}$.

CRITICAL LINCHPIN (independent): the greedy $\tau^*\subseteq P(a_j)$ is a GLOBAL minimal transversal of $\mathcal M_{j-1}$ (i.e. $\tau^*\in b(\mathcal M_{j-1})$), because any transversal contained in $\tau^*\subseteq P(a_j)$ is contained in $P(a_j)$, contradicting minimality-within-$P(a_j)$. Verified $\tau^*\in b(\mathcal M_{j-1})$ on all events for $a_1\le385$ (brute blocker) and via the single-removal characterization for $a_1\in\{777,4199,2310,249,30030,510510\}$; also 0/2000 failures on random pairwise-intersecting antichains.

Defect property: $\tau^*\in b(\mathcal M_{j-1})\setminus\mathcal M_{j-1}$ (else $P(a_j)\supseteq\tau^*\in\mathcal M_{j-1}$ would make $P(a_j)$ non-minimal, contradicting it being a new member of $\mathcal M_j$). Verified.

CB Theorem (Step 9) — the closed crux: $k\le a_1$ at every essential entry, equivalently every essential prime $\le a_1$. Proof by contradiction re-derived end-to-end and found valid: assume $k>a_1$ ($\Leftrightarrow a_{j-1}\ge a_1 D$); construct $m=Dc$ with $P(m)=\tau^*$, $a_1<m\le a_{j-1}$, $m\in V_{j-1}$; TERM $\Rightarrow m=a_s$, $P(a_s)=\tau^*$, $2\le s\le j-1$; defect $\Rightarrow B_{j-1}=\emptyset$; backward Lemma C $\Rightarrow B_{s-1}=\emptyset\Rightarrow\tau^*$ enters $\mathcal M_s\Rightarrow B_s\ne\emptyset$; forward Lemma C $\Rightarrow B_{j-1}\ne\emptyset$, contradiction. 0 CB violations for $a_1\le1500$ and on large targets incl. primorial $510510$ ($\max k/a_1=0.508$), $30030$ ($0.546$); no essential prime exceeds $a_1$ in any tested case.

Step 8 termination: CB $\Rightarrow$ every member of every $\mathcal M_n$ is a subset of the finite ground set $\{p\le a_1\}$; distinct antichains finite; $\mathcal M_n$ never revisits a value after a strict change (each change strictly shrinks $V$) $\Rightarrow$ finitely many changes $\Rightarrow$ stabilization. Verified (distinct-$\mathcal M$ count $=$ changes$+1$).

End-state self-duality: stabilized $\mathcal M$ satisfies $b(\mathcal M)=\mathcal M$ for all tested $a_1$ (independent blocker computation). Consistent with (though not strictly required by) the periodicity argument.

Refutations re-confirmed: 'essential $\le\max P(a_1)$' false ($385\to19$); 'termination by monotone $|\mathcal M_n|$' false ($2310$ grows to 251 then collapses; $249$ grows then collapses); 'no-new-prime-set detects stabilization' false (non-minimal supersets persist).
summary: COMPLETE, CORRECT proof of IMO 2026 P6 — a genuine advance over v2, which left the central crux (finitely many essential primes) open. The Cofactor Bound (CB) argument in Step 9 closes it: at every essential-prime entry the cofactor $k=\lfloor a_{j-1}/\prod\tau^*\rfloor+1$ is $\le a_1$, so every essential prime is $\le a_1$ (finite), Step 8 forces $\mathcal M_n$ to stabilize over the finite ground set $\{p\le a_1\}$, and Steps 3–4 give $a_{n+T}=a_n+L$ for every $n\ge1$. I re-derived the CB contradiction by hand and confirmed every load-bearing piece independently: the exact cofactor identity; TERM (Lemma A); smooth-gap (Lemma B); B-monotonicity (Lemma C); the critical fact that greedy $\tau^*\subseteq P(a_j)$ is a global minimal transversal (hence a defect); and CB itself with 0 violations across $a_1$ up to the primorial $510510$, with no essential prime ever exceeding $a_1$. The construction $m=Dc$ and the empty-vs-nonempty-$B_{j-1}$ contradiction are airtight. The 'for every $n$' quantifier is genuinely satisfied (period holds from $n=1$; verified). Remaining items are presentation polish (the author's verify_proof.py uses a current-step proxy for the step-$s$ blocker check and has a truncated docstring — a code-verification gap, not a proof gap) and an optional streamlining noting that periodicity does not depend on the self-dual characterization. This is a model review, not an official certificate, but the proof as written is valid.
transfer_assessment: REUSABLE: reduction of 'shares a factor with every earlier term' to 'prime-set is a transversal of the minimal family $\mathcal M_n$', and the valid set $V_n$ = union of divisibility classes over the blocker $b(\mathcal M_n)$ — a clean bridge from the greedy gcd condition to periodicity mod $L$.

REUSABLE (KEY): the Cofactor Bound proof pattern — at each 'entry' event, the entering structure is a cofactor $k=\lfloor\text{prev}/D\rfloor+1$ of a realized defect; bounding $k$ by an invariant ($a_1$) via constructing a smooth witness $m=Dc$ (Lemma B), invoking a 'universal-validity-in-range implies realized' lemma (TERM, Lemma A), and a monotone-blocker lemma (Lemma C) to force a contradiction. This contradiction template (defect forces $B=\emptyset$ but the witness's entry forces $B\ne\emptyset$) is the transferable engine.
REUSABLE: TERM lemma (any universally-valid integer in $[a_1,a_n]$ is necessarily a term) — a well-founded-ordering tool that turns a constructed witness into an actual sequence element.
REUSABLE: smooth-gap lemma (consecutive $S$-smooth numbers have ratio $\le\min S$) for bounding smooth cofactors.
REUSABLE: B-monotonicity (subset-members of a fixed target can never fully vanish once present) for propagation/contradiction across time steps.

REUSABLE: the observation that periodicity holds FROM $n=1$ (not merely eventually) because every term is a transversal of the eventual $\mathcal M$ and $V\subseteq V_n$ — correctly resolves the 'for every $n$' quantifier.

MISLEADING (minor): the self-dual fixed-point characterization (Step 6) is presented as load-bearing but is not actually needed for the theorem — periodicity follows from essential-prime finiteness + stabilization alone. A future reader should not over-invest in proving $b(\mathcal M)=\mathcal M$.
